name: Apis mellifera
habitat: Managed hives, and wild colonies in tree hollows and wall cavities.
hazard_note: Honey bees sting when their hive or swarm is disturbed. Please keep away from swarms and wild colonies. If someone has a severe allergic reaction, call 000.
description: The bee kept for honey, brought to Australia in the 1820s. It forages over several kilometres and visits most flowering plants.

name: Tetragonula carbonaria
plant_note: Collects nectar and pollen from many flowers, and resin from trees such as corymbias for building its nest.
habitat: Tree hollows and hive boxes in warm spots. It stops flying below about 18 °C.
description: A tiny black stingless bee that lives in colonies of thousands and stores a little tangy honey, called sugarbag.

name: Amegilla cingulata
plant_note: Buzz-pollinates tomatoes and eggplants, and visits blue and purple flowers such as salvias and lavender.
habitat: Nests alone in burrows dug in soft sandstone, clay banks or mud brick. Males roost at night clinging to plant stems.
description: A solitary native bee with bright metallic blue bands across a black abdomen.

name: Amegilla bombiformis
plant_note: Buzz-pollinates flowers such as tomatoes and hibbertias.
habitat: Nests alone in burrows in soil banks.
description: A furry golden-brown solitary bee with a buzzy, darting flight.

name: Xylocopa bombylans
plant_note: Nests in soft wood, such as dead banksia trees, cutting its own entrance holes with its strong jaws.
habitat: Urban areas, forests, woodlands and heath in eastern Australia north of Sydney. Its nest is usually a single tunnel about 30 cm long.
description: A large carpenter bee, about 1.6 to 1.8 cm long, whose metallic colours shift from purple to yellowy green in the light. It drones deeply as it flies.

name: Leioproctus plumosus
habitat: Urban areas with sandy ground, forests, woodlands and heath. Each female digs her own tunnel in sandy ground, and many tunnels can be close together.
description: A very hairy solitary bee, 8 to 14 mm long, with a metallic green-blue body. In spring the males, which cannot sting, gather over the nesting ground.

name: Megachile
plant_note: Cuts neat round holes in soft leaves, such as rose leaves, to line its nest.
habitat: Urban areas, forests, woodlands and heath. Leafcutter bees are common in Sydney gardens.
description: Solitary bees 5 to 14 mm long. Females have strong jaws for cutting leaves, a large head and a stout abdomen, and some kinds build their nests with resin instead.

name: Hylaeus
plant_note: One kind gathers in large numbers around flowering eucalypts and angophoras.
habitat: Urban areas, forests, woodlands and heath. Many kinds nest in twigs, branches and reeds.
description: Small bees, 3 to 11 mm long, named for the yellow or white markings on their faces. Australia has more kinds of masked bee than anywhere else in the world.

name: Nomia
habitat: Urban areas, forests, woodlands and heath. Most kinds nest in the ground, and up to three females can share a burrow, taking turns to guard it. At night the males cling to grass stems.
description: Bees about 1 cm long. A common kind is dark brown with golden bands, and the green and gold Nomia bee has white and golden hairs on a metallic blue-green abdomen.

name: Lasioglossum
habitat: Urban areas, forests, woodlands and heath. Most kinds nest in the ground, and some females share the entrance of a burrow, each digging her own tunnel off its main passage.
description: Medium-sized bees about 1 cm long, black or dark brown with broad bands of white hair across the abdomen.

name: Papilio aegeus
plant_note: Its caterpillars feed on citrus and murraya leaves. A few rarely harm a healthy tree, so they can be left or moved by hand.
habitat: Gardens with citrus trees and nectar flowers.
description: A large black butterfly; females have white and red markings. Young caterpillars look like bird droppings and older ones are green, and they push out an orange, smelly horn when disturbed.

name: Danaus plexippus
plant_note: Its caterpillars feed only on milkweeds.
habitat: Gardens and roadsides where milkweeds grow.
description: A large orange butterfly with black veins and white spots that reached Australia in the 1870s.

name: Belenois java
plant_note: Its caterpillars feed on native caper bushes. In some springs, adults migrate in great numbers.
habitat: Inland scrub with caper bushes, and gardens along its migration routes.
description: A white butterfly with black wing edges and yellow-orange patches beneath.

name: Euploea corinna
plant_note: Its caterpillars feed on figs, oleander and native vines.
habitat: Warm gardens and forest edges.
description: A dark brown butterfly with white spots along its wing edges.

name: Graphium choredon
plant_note: Its caterpillars feed on camphor laurel and native laurels.
habitat: Gardens and rainforest edges.
description: A fast-flying black swallowtail with a band of bright blue triangles across its wings.

name: Pieris rapae
plant_note: Its green caterpillars eat cabbage, broccoli and other brassicas, and nasturtiums.
habitat: Vegetable gardens.
description: A white butterfly with one or two black spots on each forewing, introduced from Europe.

name: Coccinella transversalis
plant_note: Adults and larvae eat aphids.
habitat: Gardens with aphids and flowers.
description: A small orange ladybird with black zigzag markings.

name: Illeis galbula
plant_note: Adults and larvae eat powdery mildew on leaves.
habitat: Plants with powdery mildew, such as pumpkins and zinnias.
description: A small yellow ladybird with black markings.

name: Nezara viridula
plant_note: Sucks sap from beans, tomatoes and other vegetables, leaving marks on pods and fruit.
habitat: Vegetable gardens.
description: A green shield bug. Its young are black with white, red and yellow spots.

name: Musgraveia sulciventris
plant_note: Sucks sap from new citrus shoots, which can make flowers and young fruit drop. It squirts a liquid that burns the eyes, so please wear gloves and eye protection when you remove it.
habitat: Citrus trees.
description: A large bronze to black stink bug; its young are green to orange and flat.

name: Bactrocera tryoni
plant_note: Lays eggs in ripening fruit and fruiting vegetables, and its maggots spoil the fruit.
habitat: Gardens with fruit trees and fruiting vegetables in warm months.
description: A reddish-brown fly with yellow markings, smaller than a house fly.

name: Myzus persicae
plant_note: Sucks sap from new growth and spreads plant viruses. Ladybirds, hover fly larvae and lacewings eat it.
habitat: Soft new growth on vegetables and flowers.
description: A small pale green to pink aphid that gathers in colonies under leaves.

name: Vespula germanica
habitat: Nests mostly underground, and in walls and roof spaces.
hazard_note: European wasps can sting many times and defend their nest fiercely. Please keep away from the nest. If someone has a severe allergic reaction, call 000.

rules.text: European wasps are a declared pest in Western Australia. Please report one to the Pest and Disease Information Service on 08 9368 3080, or through MyPestGuide Reporter, and leave the nest for the department to destroy.

description: A yellow-and-black wasp with completely black antennae that tucks its legs up as it flies. It scavenges meat and sweet food in summer.

name: Polistes humilis
plant_note: Hunts caterpillars to feed its young.
habitat: Small open nests of grey paper under eaves and in shrubs.
hazard_note: Paper wasps sting when their nest is disturbed. Please keep away from the nest.
description: A slender brown-and-yellow wasp that dangles its legs as it flies.

name: Solenopsis invicta
habitat: Nests in open, sunny ground such as lawns, as flat mounds of loose soil with no entry holes.
hazard_note: Fire ants swarm and sting many times. Please keep children and pets away from the nest. If someone has a severe allergic reaction, call 000.

rules.text: Fire ants must be reported straight away. Please call 13 22 68 (132 ANT) or report them online at fireants.org.au.
Fire ants must be reported straight away. Please call the NSW Biosecurity Helpline on 1800 680 244 or use the department's online form, and do not treat the nest yourself.

description: A small coppery-brown ant with a darker abdomen, from South America. Workers vary in size within one nest.

name: Orthodera ministralis
plant_note: Hunts flies, moths and other insects among flowers and leaves.
habitat: Shrubs and flowers.
description: A bright green praying mantis with a wide, shield-like thorax.

name: Ischiodon scutellaris
plant_note: Adults feed on nectar and pollen from small flowers; the larvae eat aphids.
habitat: Gardens with small open flowers such as alyssum, coriander and daisies.
description: A small fly with yellow and black bands that hovers in place over flowers. It does not sting.
